short.q: Write the meaning of the first verse of Surah Al-Ikhlas, "Qul huwallahu ahad".
short.answer: Say: He is Allah, the One.
short.working: 1 mark for "Say" and 1 mark for "Allah is One".

short.q: Why are Al-Falaq and An-Naas called the two surahs of seeking refuge?
short.answer: Both begin with "Qul a'udhu", meaning "Say: I seek refuge". In them we ask Allah to protect us from harm.
short.working: 1 mark for the opening words, 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for protection.

short.q: Match each surah with one lesson: Al-Fatiha, Al-Kafirun, An-Nasr and Al-Ikhlas.
short.answer: Al-Fatiha: praise Allah and ask for guidance; Al-Kafirun: stay firm in faith; An-Nasr: thank Allah when you succeed; Al-Ikhlas: Allah is One.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair.

short.q: Give three character traits of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and one way to practise each.
short.answer: Trustworthy: return borrowed items. Truthful: tell the truth about mistakes. Kind: share your lunch.
short.working: 1 mark for each trait with a suitable way.

short.q: State the hadith of eating that is in your syllabus.
short.answer: Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat what is directly in front of you.
short.working: 1 mark for the first two teachings and 1 mark for the third, or 1 mark each for correct halves.

short.q: Explain what a person should do if they do not like a food served to them.
short.answer: Leave it quietly and politely without criticising, as the Prophet did, and thank the person.
short.working: 1 mark for not criticising, 1 mark for quietness or politeness, 1 mark for thanks.

short.q: Explain how not brushing teeth can harm them.
short.answer: Food and sugar stay on the teeth, germs turn them into acid, and acid makes cavities which cause toothache and bad breath.
short.working: 1 mark for each of the four steps or harms.

short.q: Explain the meaning of "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both."
short.answer: Both types have good because of faith. But a strong believer can do more good, so a Muslim should try to be strong in body and faith.
short.working: 1 mark for good in both, 1 mark for strong can do more good, 1 mark for the lesson.

short.q: Plan a Muslim school sports day including at least five rules or activities.
short.answer: Bismillah at the start, modest kits, fair play, warm-up, stop for prayer, respect referees, greet teams, thank Allah at the end.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid rule or activity, up to 5.

short.q: Write a dua using two of Allah's names and explain why you chose them.
short.answer: For example: "Ya Rahman, Ya Rahim, forgive me and have mercy on me", because I need mercy.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct name, 1 mark for the request, 1 mark for the reason.

short.q: State the duties of Jibril, Mikail and Israfil.
short.answer: Jibril brings revelation, Mikail is in charge of rain and provision, Israfil will blow the Trumpet.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Write the six pillars of Iman and put a mark next to the one studied in this lesson.
short.answer: Belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and destiny. Angels are the one studied.
short.working: 1 mark for every two pillars named, 1 mark for identifying angels.

short.q: Explain how Prophet Ayyub (A.S.) showed patience.
short.answer: He was tested with illness and loss. He did not complain against Allah, called upon Him, and Allah healed him.
short.working: 1 mark for the test, 1 mark for not complaining, 1 mark for calling upon Allah.

short.q: Describe how a Grade 4 child can practise honesty, generosity, patience and obedience.
short.answer: Honesty: return lost items; generosity: share lunch; patience: wait calmly for a turn; obedience: come when parents call.
short.working: 1 mark for each virtue with a suitable action.

short.q: Give one example of each type of najasa.
short.answer: Light: urine of a baby boy on milk only; medium: urine, stool, blood or vomit; heavy: dog or pig saliva.
short.working: 1 mark for each example.

short.q: How should a Muslim treat dogs even though their saliva is heavy najasa?
short.answer: Kindly, without cruelty, giving them food and water, and only being careful to avoid their saliva.
short.working: 1 mark for kindness, 1 mark for not cruel, 1 mark for careful with saliva.

short.q: Explain the rule when you are unsure whether wudhu broke.
short.answer: If you were sure you made wudhu and only doubt it broke, you remain in wudhu, because certainty is not removed by doubt.
short.working: 1 mark for staying in wudhu, 1 mark for certainty, 1 mark for the example.

short.q: What must a boy and what must a girl cover in prayer at the least?
short.answer: A boy must cover from the navel to the knees. A girl must cover the whole body except the face and hands.
short.working: 1 mark for the boy, 1 mark for the girl, 1 mark for the general rule of modest clothes.

short.q: Why do Muslims all over the world face the Qibla?
short.answer: Allah commanded it in the Qur'an (2:144). It unites Muslims and shows that we worship one Lord.
short.working: 1 mark for command, 1 mark for the verse or Kaaba, 1 mark for unity, 1 mark for one Lord.

short.q: What do we say in ruku, in sujud and when sitting between the two sujud?
short.answer: Ruku: Subhana Rabbiyal Azim; sujud: Subhana Rabbiyal A'la; sitting: Rabbighfir li.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain the lesson from the story of the man who gave a dog water.
short.answer: A small act of kindness can earn Allah's forgiveness and reward, and there is reward in serving every living creature.
short.working: 1 mark for kindness, 1 mark for forgiveness, 1 mark for all creatures.

short.q: Describe how a class can show kindness to creatures in the school compound.
short.answer: Plant and water trees, put out water for birds, keep the compound clean, do not harm insects and animals.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid action.

short.q: Give three benefits of the Islamic dress code.
short.answer: Protection, dignity and respect, trains modesty and self-control, obedience to Allah.
short.working: 1 mark for each benefit.

short.q: Give three negative uses of media.
short.answer: Watching harmful content, wasting time, spreading rumours, cyberbullying, unsafe contacts.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: State three groups of people who deserve help.
short.answer: People in debt, people who lost property through disaster, and the destitute.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Suggest three honest ways of earning a living.
short.answer: Farming, trading in a kiosk, tailoring, carpentry, teaching.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: State three benefits of saying the duas for leaving and entering the house.
short.answer: Protection, remembering Allah, blessings and peace, following the Sunnah, building good habits.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain why parents should be fair among their children.
short.answer: The Prophet told parents to fear Allah and be fair among children. Favouring one causes jealousy and hurt.
short.working: 1 mark for the teaching, 1 mark for jealousy, 1 mark for fairness.

short.q: Role-play plan: Write a short scene showing a parent fulfilling one obligation and the child's thanks.
short.answer: A parent helps with homework and the child says thank you and promises to do well. Award for a clear obligation, a clear action and an expression of thanks.
short.working: 1 mark for the obligation, 1 mark for the action, 1 mark for thanks, 2 marks for clarity.

short.q: When must a child not obey a parent, and how should the child still behave?
short.answer: When a parent commands something Allah forbids. The child should still treat them kindly and politely.
short.working: 1 mark for the case, 1 mark for not obeying, 1 mark for kindness.

short.q: State three duties to grandparents.
short.answer: Respect and greet them, help them, visit them, listen to their stories, make dua.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: What should a child do when two cousins quarrel?
short.answer: Stay calm, encourage them to forgive and make peace, and ask an elder if needed.
short.working: 1 mark for calm, 1 mark for peace, 1 mark for asking elders.

short.q: Write the meaning of the first two verses of Surah Al-Alaq.
short.answer: Read in the name of your Lord who created; He created man from a clinging clot.
short.working: 1 mark for each verse.

short.q: Who were the three earliest converts studied in this lesson?
short.answer: Khadija, Ali and Abu Bakr.
short.working: 1 mark for two names and 1 mark for the third.

short.q: Explain why the earliest converts are important.
short.answer: They believed when it was hard, supported the Prophet morally and materially, and encouraged others.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid point.

short.q: State three virtues the Prophet showed in Taif.
short.answer: Patience, tolerance, perseverance, mercy, trust in Allah.
short.working: 1 mark for each.
